title: tshark: Restore deprecated default column field titles
description:
Restore the ability in tshark -e to filter based on column titles,
at least for the seven default columns.  Internally alias the fields
based on their titles to the column type based fields, e.g.
"_ws.col.Info" to "_ws.col.info"

This may be removed in the future, but is useful to have as there
are tools and scripts that use the old behavior (and there are
supported versions, 3.6.x and 4.0.x that only support the old
behavior.)

notes.body: mentioned in merge request !10513

That works, but to avoid repeating the prefix name, you could also consider this convenience function:
```suggestion:-0+0
    if (g_str_has_prefix(field, COLUMN_FIELD_FILTER)) {
```

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11752/diffs?diff_id=765238806&start_sha=8cb6098e9a190b288fcc4e1458f2f5db7b2715f7#b388b8746f4c394b12d02cd5401973d2b221485d_2115_2115)

I would prefer if we keep supporting this for ever, not print a warning. We could internally alias the default fields at parsing time, for example from `_ws.col.Info` to `_ws.col.info`, and so on.

Unless there is a strong technical reason to change this, I would be in favor of maintaining backwards compatibility.
Several tools rely on the interface that remained stable for years:
https://github.com/search?q=%22_ws.col%22&type=code

Doing it when parsing in tshark does make sense... One thing is that we don't have a generic field alias function, only one for protocol functions. It might be fine to introduce an internal function just for aliasing the column fields.
Do you want to continue to support (in tshark -e, not anywhere else) non-default column titles, or are the default ones enough?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/11752/diffs?diff_id=765238806&start_sha=8cb6098e9a190b288fcc4e1458f2f5db7b2715f7#b388b8746f4c394b12d02cd5401973d2b221485d_2131_2124)

The default columns are sufficient for me, I don't need custom columns. Like you said, referencing the fields is superior. There are cases where that is not possible though. In particular, `_ws.col.Info` is documented in the TShark manual and `tshark --help` output.

Since the Info column (and to some extent, the Protocol) columns are pretty unique, I can see why people would like to add it to a `tshark -Tfields` output.

Example from [the official Zeek (formerly Bro) docs](https://github.com/zeek/zeek-docs/blob/0270f098d712b0d090a1cf1d3d6f3c27557c88ac/logs/smb.rst#reviewing-the-packet-capture-with-programtshark), word-wrapped for easier reading:
```
$ tshark -r 20171220_smb_at_schedule.pcap -T fields -e _ws.col.No. \
    -e _ws.col.Source -e _ws.col.Protocol -e _ws.col.Info -Y smb2
```

Another example, interestingly it is using `-Tfields` as well instead of `-Tjson`. https://github.com/ddos-clearing-house/ddos_dissector/blob/3ee90caf91194f5f460feac30c1a96dfae1c5d8a/src/reader.py#L32-L57
```
PCAP_COLUMN_NAMES: dict[str, str] = {
    'ip.dst': 'destination_address',
    'ip.src': 'source_address',
    'tcp.flags.str': 'tcp_flags',
    'ip.proto': 'protocol',
    '_ws.col.Destination': 'col_destination_address',
    '_ws.col.Source': 'col_source_address',
    '_ws.col.Protocol': 'service',
    'dns.qry.name': 'dns_query_name',
    'dns.qry.type': 'dns_query_type',
    'eth.type': 'ethernet_type',
    'frame.len': 'nr_bytes',
    'udp.length': 'udp_length',
    'http.request.uri': 'http_uri',
    'http.request.method': 'http_method',
    'http.user_agent': 'http_user_agent',
    'icmp.type': 'icmp_type',
    'ip.frag_offset': 'fragmentation_offset',
    'ip.ttl': 'ttl',
    'ntp.priv.reqcode': 'ntp_requestcode',
    'tcp.dstport': 'tcp_destination_port',
    'tcp.srcport': 'tcp_source_port',
    'udp.dstport': 'udp_destination_port',
    'udp.srcport': 'udp_source_port',
    '_ws.col.Time': 'time_start'
}
```

And someone trying to reproduce the default columns layout,
https://github.com/Orange-OpenSource/dynagraph/blob/7ce18cf49a765645f3cfc1d80690931938c8a594/data-collection/README.md?plain=1#L56C6-L63
```
# Capture net traffic, export data as CSV, transform it to json, send it
# Press Ctrl-C to stop the process
tshark -T fields -l -E separator=, -E quote=d \
  -e _ws.col.No. -e _ws.col.Time \
  -e _ws.col.Source -e _ws.col.Destination \
  -e _ws.col.Protocol -e _ws.col.Length -e _ws.col.Info \
  -r ../samples/open_github_wireshark_2021-09-04_16-52-21.pcapng | \
  python ws_server_stdin.py
```
Hey John, thanks for working on this. I am not sure if I agree with changing the interface, but I am curious to hear your thoughts!

Another thing that I'm not completely satisfied with are some of the name for the "default" columns (as in not specifying resolved or unresolved, but using the prefs.) I copied for the filter fields from the internal names, but I'm not sure that, e.g., `_ws.col.def_dst` is really superior to just `_ws.col.dst`.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -199,9 +199,13 @@ The following features are new (or have been significantly updated) since versio
 
 * With the addition of the universal and consistent filtering support for
 column text, the previous support in the -e option to tshark for displaying
-column text via the column title, e.g. "_ws.col.Info", has been removed.
-The previous implementation allowed names that are not legal filter names
-and wsbuglink:16576[silently ignored columns that didn't exist.]
+column text via the column title has been removed in general. Those field names
+cannot be used elsewhere (as they may not be legal filter names) and create
+confusion if more than one column has the same title or if a column is renamed.
+Prefer the column format instead, e.g. "_ws.col.info" for "_ws.col.Info".
+However, for backwards compatibilty with existing tools and scripts, the
+titles of the default columns can continue to be used with "tshark -e"
+(but not elsewhere.)
 
 * The bundled script "dtd_gen.lua" that was disabled by default has been removed
   from the installation. It can be found in the Wireshark Wiki under "Contrib".

@@ -120,6 +120,16 @@ gboolean parse_column_format(fmt_data *cfmt, const char *fmt);
 WS_DLL_PUBLIC
 void try_convert_to_custom_column(char **fmt);
 
+/** Checks a column field string to see if it is a name of a filter
+ * field created using a default column title (as used in tshark -e),
+ * and alias it to the new column type based field.
+ *
+ * @param[in] field The old title based field, e.g. "_ws.col.Info"
+ * @return The new field, e.g. "_ws.col.info", or NULL
+ */
+WS_DLL_PUBLIC
+const char* try_convert_to_column_field(const char *field);
+
